Migrate this Next.js project from Pages Router to App Router. The project currently uses the pages directory structure with two pages (index and about). You need to:

1. Create the app directory with the proper App Router structure
2. Migrate the pages from pages/ to app/ (index → app/page.tsx, about → app/about/page.tsx)
3. Create a root layout file (app/layout.tsx) with proper HTML structure and shared metadata
4. Remove the pages directory and any pages-specific files
5. Update imports and routing patterns to use App Router conventions
6. Ensure the migrated app builds and runs correctly

Keep the same functionality and UI, but use App Router patterns and file structure.

history.assistant:
The project is now on the App Router. next build completed successfully (exit 0) and prerendered / and /about.

What changed:

- pages/index.tsx became app/page.tsx, and pages/about.tsx became app/about/page.tsx.
- pages/_app.tsx and pages/_document.tsx were replaced by app/layout.tsx, which owns the <html lang="en"> and <body> shell plus shared metadata (title, description, favicon). The viewport meta tag is added by Next.js automatically.
- Page titles and descriptions now come from the Metadata API instead of next/head.
- Internal links use next/link instead of raw <a> tags.
- The pages directory was removed.

Next.js also updated tsconfig.json during the build to include .next/dev/types//.ts.

Hello Next.js!

38 } 39 ``` 40 41 ## Creating a layout 42 43 A layout is UI that is **shared** between multiple pages. On navigation, layouts preserve state, remain interactive, and do not rerender. 44 45 You can define a layout by default exporting a React component from a [`layout` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout). 18 	
19 	The Metadata APIs can be used to define your application metadata for improved SEO and web shareability and include:
20 	
21 	1. [The static `metadata` object](#static-metadata)
22 	2. [The dynamic `generateMetadata` function](#generated-metadata)
23 	3. Special [file conventions](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) that can be used to add static or dynamically generated [favicons](#favicons) and [OG images](#static-open-graph-images).
24 	
25 	With all the options above, Next.js will automatically generate the relevant `<head>` tags for your page, which can be inspected in the browser's developer tools.
26 	
27 	The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are only supported in Server Components.
28 	
29 	## Default fields
30 	
31 	There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
32 	
33 	- The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
34 	- The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
35 	
36 	```html
37 	<meta charset="utf-8" />
38 	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
39 	```
40 	
41 	The other metadata fields can be defined with the `Metadata` object (for [static metadata](#static-metadata)) or the `generateMetadata` function (for [generated metadata](#generated-metadata)).
42 	
43 	## Static metadata
44 	
45 	To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-object) from a static [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) or [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) file. For example, to add a title and description to the blog route:
46 	
47 	```tsx filename="app/blog/layout.tsx" switcher
48 	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
49 	
50 	export const metadata: Metadata = {
51 	  title: 'My Blog',
52 	  description: '...',
53 	}
54 	
55 	export default function Layout() {}
56 	```
57 	
58 	```jsx filename="app/blog/layout.js" switcher
59 	export const metadata = {
60 	  title: 'My Blog',
61 	  description: '...',
62 	}
63 	
64 	export default function Layout() {}
65 	```
66 	
67 	You can view a full list of available options, in the [`generateMetadata` documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#metadata-fields).
68 	
69 	## Generated metadata
70 	
71 	You can use [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) function to `fetch` metadata that depends on data. For example, to fetch the title and description for a specific blog post:
72 	
73 	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
74 	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
75 	
76 	type Props = {
77 	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
78 	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
79 	}
80 	
81 	export async function generateMetadata(
82 	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
83 	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
84 	): Promise<Metadata> {
85 	  const slug = (await params).slug
86 	
87 	  // fetch post information
88 	  const post = await fetch(`https://api.vercel.app/blog/${slug}`).then((res) =>
89 	    res.json()
90 	  )
91 	
92 	  return {
93 	    title: post.title,
94 	    description: post.description,
95 	  }
96 	}
97 	
98 	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
99 	```
100	
101	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
102	export async function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }, parent) {
103	  const slug = (await params).slug
104	
105	  // fetch post information
106	  const post = await fetch(`https://api.vercel.app/blog/${slug}`).then((res) =>
107	    res.json()
108	  )
109	
110	  return {
111	    title: post.title,
112	    description: post.description,

119	### Streaming metadata
120	
121	For dynamically rendered pages, Next.js streams metadata separately, injecting it into the HTML once `generateMetadata` resolves, without blocking UI rendering.
122	
123	Streaming metadata improves perceived performance by allowing visual content to stream first.
124	
125	Streaming metadata is **disabled for bots and crawlers** that expect metadata to be in the `<head>` tag (e.g. `Twitterbot`, `Slackbot`, `Bingbot`). These are detected by using the User Agent header from the incoming request.
126	
127	You can customize or **disable** streaming metadata completely, with the [`htmlLimitedBots`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/htmlLimitedBots#disabling) option in your Next.js config file.
128	
129	Prerendered pages don’t use streaming since metadata is resolved at build time.
130	
131	Learn more about [streaming metadata](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata).
132	
133	### Memoizing data requests
134	
135	There may be cases where you need to fetch the **same** data for metadata and the page itself. To avoid duplicate requests, you can use React's [`cache` function](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) to memoize the return value and only fetch the data once. Next.js comes with built-in [prefetching](#prefetching), [streaming](#streaming), and [client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions) ensuring navigation stays fast and responsive. 13 14 This guide explains how navigation works in Next.js and how you can optimize it for [dynamic routes](#dynamic-routes-without-loadingtsx) and [slow networks](#slow-networks). 15 16 ## How navigation works 17 18 To understand how navigation works in Next.js, it helps to be familiar with the following concepts: 19 20 - [Server Rendering](#server-rendering) 21 - [Prefetching](#prefetching) 22 - [Streaming](#streaming) 23 - [Client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions) 24 25 ### Server Rendering 26 27 In Next.js, [Layouts and Pages](/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages) are [React Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components) by default. On initial and subsequent navigations, the [Server Component Payload](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#how-do-server-and-client-components-work-in-nextjs) is generated on the server before being sent to the client. 28 29 There are two types of server rendering, based on _when_ it happens: 30 31 - **Prerendering** happens at build time or during [revalidation](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) and the result is cached. 32 - **Dynamic Rendering** happens at request time in response to a client request. 33 34 The trade-off of server rendering is that the client must wait for the server to respond before the new route can be shown. Next.js addresses this delay by [prefetching](#prefetching) routes the user is likely to visit and performing [client-side transitions](#client-side-transitions). 35 36 > **Good to know**: HTML is also generated for the initial visit. 37 38 ### Prefetching 39 40 Prefetching is the process of loading a route in the background before the user navigates to it. This makes navigation between routes in your application feel instant, because by the time a user clicks on a link, the data to render the next route is already available client side. 41 42 Next.js automatically prefetches routes linked with the [`` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) when they enter the user's viewport. 43 44 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 45 import Link from 'next/link' 46 47 export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 48 return ( 49 50 51
52 {/* Prefetched when the link is hovered or enters the viewport */} 53 Blog 54 {/* No prefetching */} 55 Contact 56
57 {children} 58 59 60 ) 61 } 62 ``` 63 64 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 65 import Link from 'next/link' 66 67 export default function Layout({ children }) { 68 return ( 69 70 71
72 {/* Prefetched when the link is hovered or enters the viewport */} 73 Blog 74 {/* No prefetching */} 75 Contact 76
77 {children} 78 79 80 ) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 How much of the route is prefetched depends on whether it's static or dynamic: 85 86 - **Static Route**: the full route is prefetched. 87 - **Dynamic Route**: prefetching is skipped, or the route is partially prefetched if [`loading.tsx`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) is present. 88 89 By skipping or partially prefetching dynamic routes, Next.js avoids unnecessary work on the server for routes the users may never visit. However, waiting for a server response before navigation can give the users the impression that the app is not responding. 90 91 98 99 > **Good to know:** See the [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) for the full behavior, including how to control prefetching per link and how it changes when you adopt [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). To include URL-dependent content in a link's prefetch, see [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching). 100 101 To improve the navigation experience to dynamic routes, you can use [streaming](#streaming). 102 103 ### Streaming 104 105 Streaming allows the server to send parts of a dynamic route to the client as soon as they're ready, rather than waiting for the entire route to be rendered. This means users see something sooner, even if parts of the page are still loading. See the [Streaming guide](/docs/app/guides/streaming) for a deep dive into how streaming works in Next.js. 106 107 For dynamic routes, it means they can be **partially prefetched**. 1  	---
2  	title: layout.js
3  	description: API reference for the layout.js file.
4  	---
5  	
6  	The `layout` file is used to define a layout in your Next.js application.
7  	
8  	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher
9  	export default function DashboardLayout({
10 	  children,
11 	}: {
12 	  children: React.ReactNode
13 	}) {
14 	  return <section>{children}</section>
15 	}
16 	```
17 	
18 	```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher
19 	export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) {
20 	  return <section>{children}</section>
21 	}
22 	```
23 	
24 	In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `layout.js` is the outermost component in a route segment. It wraps `template.js`, `error.js`, `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, and `page.js`.
25 	
26 	A **root layout** is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. It is used to define the `<html>` and `<body>` tags and other globally shared UI.
27 	
28 	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
29 	export default function RootLayout({
30 	  children,
31 	}: {
32 	  children: React.ReactNode
33 	}) {
34 	  return (
35 	    <html lang="en">
36 	      <body>{children}</body>
37 	    </html>
38 	  )
39 	}
40 	```
41 	
42 	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
43 	export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
44 	  return (
45 	    <html lang="en">
46 	      <body>{children}</body>
47 	    </html>
48 	  )
49 	}
50 	```
51 	
52 	## Reference
53 	
54 	### Props
55 	
56 	#### `children` (required)
57 	
58 	Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable.
59 	
60 	#### `params` (optional)
61 	
62 	A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to that layout.
63 	
64 	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.tsx" switcher
65 	export default async function Layout({
66 	  children,
67 	  params,
68 	}: {
69 	  children: React.ReactNode
70 	  params: Promise<{ team: string }>
71 	}) {
72 	  const { team } = await params
73 	}
74 	```
75 	
76 	```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher
77 	export default async function Layout({ children, params }) {
78 	  const { team } = await params
79 	}
80 	```
81 	
82 	| Example Route                     | URL            | `params`                           |
83 	| --------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
84 	| `app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
85 	| `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/layout.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
86 	| `app/blog/[...slug]/layout.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |
87 	
88 	- Since the `params` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values.
89 	  - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
90 	
91 	### Layout Props Helper
92 	
93 	You can type layouts with `LayoutProps` to get a strongly typed `params` and named slots inferred from your directory structure. `LayoutProps` is a globally available helper.
94 	
95 	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx"
96 	export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<'/dashboard'>) {
97 	  return (
98 	    <section>
99 	      {props.children}
100	      {/* If you have app/dashboard/@analytics, it appears as a typed slot: */}
101	      {/* {props.analytics} */}
102	    </section>
103	  )
104	}
105	```
106	
107	> **Good to know**:
108	>
109	> - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`.
110	> - After type generation, the `LayoutProps` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.
111	
112	### Root Layout
113	
114	The `app` directory **must** include a **root layout**, which is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. Typically, the root layout is `app/layout.js`.
115	
116	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
117	export default function RootLayout({
118	  children,
119	}: {
120	  children: React.ReactNode
121	}) {
122	  return (
123	    <html>
124	      <body>{children}</body>
125	    </html>
126	  )
127	}
128	```
129	
130	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
131	export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
132	  return (
133	    <html>
134	      <body>{children}</body>
135	    </html>
136	  )
137	}
138	```
139	
140	- The root layout **must** define `<html>` and `<body>` tags.
141	  - You should **not** manually add `<head>` tags such as `<title>` and `<meta>` to root layouts. Instead, you should use the [Metadata API](/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images) which automatically handles advanced requirements such as streaming and de-duplicating `<head>` elements.
142	- You can create **multiple root layouts**. Any layout without a `layout.js` above it is a root layout. Two common approaches:
143	  - Using [route groups](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups) like `app/(shop)/layout.js` and `app/(marketing)/layout.js`
144	  - Omitting `app/layout.js` so layouts in subdirectories like `app/dashboard/layout.js` and `app/blog/layout.js` each become root layouts for their respective directories.
145	  - Navigating **across multiple root layouts** will cause a **full page load** (as opposed to a client-side navigation).
146	- The root layout can be under a **dynamic segment**, for example when implementing [internationalization](/docs/app/guides/internationalization) with `app/[lang]/layout.js`. Dynamic segments before the root layout are **root parameters** and can be read from any Server Component with [`next/root-params`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params).
147

4 	related:

11	---
12	
13	## Latest version
14	
15	To update to the latest version of Next.js, you can use the `upgrade` command:
16	
17	```bash package="pnpm"
18	pnpm next upgrade
19	```
20	
21	```bash package="npm"
22	npx next upgrade
23	```
24	
25	```bash package="yarn"
26	yarn next upgrade
27	```
28	
29	```bash package="bun"
30	bunx next upgrade
31	```
32	
33	Versions before Next.js 16.1.0 do not support the `upgrade` command and need to use a separate package instead:
34	
35	```bash filename="Terminal"
36	npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
37	```
38	
39	If you prefer to upgrade manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions:
40	
41	```bash package="pnpm"
42	pnpm i next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest eslint-config-next@latest
43	```
44	
45	```bash package="npm"
46	npm i next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest eslint-config-next@latest
47	```
48	
49	```bash package="yarn"
50	yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest eslint-config-next@latest
51	```
52	
53	```bash package="bun"
54	bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest eslint-config-next@latest
55	```
56	
57	## Canary version
58	
59	To update to the latest canary, make sure you're on the latest version of Next.js and everything is working as expected. Then, run the following command:
60	
61	```bash package="pnpm"
62	pnpm add next@canary
63	```
64	
65	```bash package="npm"
66	npm i next@canary
67	```
68	
69	```bash package="yarn"
70	yarn add next@canary
71	```
72	
73	```bash package="bun"
74	bun add next@canary
75	```
76	
77	### Features available in canary
78	
79	The following features are currently available in canary:
80	
81	**Authentication**:
82	
83	- [`forbidden`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/forbidden)
84	- [`unauthorized`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unauthorized)
85	- [`forbidden.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/forbidden)
86	- [`unauthorized.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/unauthorized)
87	- [`authInterrupts`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts)
